blogs.title: The 'Hawaii' Doctrine and the Limits of Judicial Review in Refugee Policy
blogs.description: This post analyzes the Ninth Circuit’s heavy reliance on the 'exudes deference' standard established in Trump v. Hawaii. It explores the implications of the court's refusal to conduct a 'searching inquiry' into the President's findings of 'detriment' under 8 U.S.C. § 1182(f), and whether this creates a nearly unreviewable zone for executive actions regarding the USRAP.

blogs.title: Authorization vs. Mandate: A Textualist Tussle Over 8 U.S.C. § 1522
blogs.description: Focusing on Judge Lee's partial dissent, this post examines the doctrinal tension between 'permissive' and 'mandatory' statutory language. It compares the majority's interpretation of 'shall' as a command to provide resettlement services with Lee's textualist argument that the statute serves as a mere 'authorization' for executive discretion.

blogs.title: Administrative Law and the Boundaries of Executive De-funding
blogs.description: This post explores the court's reasoning regarding the Administrative Procedure Act (APA) and the government's ability to abruptly terminate cooperative agreements for refugee services. It analyzes the court's finding that specific statutory requirements for 'reception and placement' services may limit the scope of executive order-driven funding shifts.
